property_summary: The reference contract always returns a non-empty version string from version(), whereas the mutant can return an empty string for some inputs; thus for every call the reference's version() returns a non-empty bytes length, and the mutant violates that for some fuzzed calldata/selector variants.

For every calldata input (bytes) passed to the external function selector of version(), the reference contract's external call completes and returns a non-empty string, whereas the mutant can return an empty string for some calldata inputs (same selector with arbitrary extra calldata).

For any bytes calldata passed via a low-level external call to c.version(), the reference contract always returns a non-empty string (length > 0) without reverting; the mutant returns an empty string for some calldata, violating that rule.

For any arbitrary bytes calldata sent via a low-level external call to c.version(), the reference C always returns a non-empty string (length > 0); the mutant that returns "" violates this because for some calldata the returned string is empty.

For any call, the reference contract always returns the semantic version string starting with '1.' (specifically "1.0.0"); the mutant returns a different string (e.g. "x") for some inputs, so asserting that the returned string's first byte equals '1' holds for the reference for all inputs but fails on the mutant for some fuzzed calldata choices.

For any caller and any inputs, only the DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT may successfully call setL1BlockValues on the reference C (so number changes only when msg.sender == DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT); the mutant allowing only address(0) breaks this by permitting non-depositor callers (i.e., callers other than DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT) to fail the restriction or allow address(0) which the fuzzer can distinguish via caller behavior.

For every caller address, reference C only allows the designated DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT to successfully call setL1BlockValues; the mutant instead only allows address(0), so there exist caller addresses for which the reference accepts the call but the mutant rejects it (or vice versa).
Only the designated depositor address can change the contract's timestamp via setL1BlockValues (i.e., timestamp can only be updated when msg.sender equals DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT).

property_summary: For every call to setL1BlockValues, the contract's public timestamp must equal the _timestamp argument passed; the mutant wrongly sets timestamp = _number so for inputs where _timestamp != _number the mutant will violate this.
